acceptance: A confirmed adopted-project Profile validates with the lite calibration level, explicit src/** and tests/** boundaries, and no blocking unknowns.
Coverage Guard production/test paths match the confirmed Profile boundaries: src/** and tests/**.
Makefile.ai.stack contains non-placeholder formatter, test, and lint commands that match the Rust project checks.
GitHub Actions runs make ai-cockpit-quality on repository changes and make check-ai-pr with the pull request base SHA.
CODEOWNERS and SECURITY.md provide non-placeholder adopter ownership and private vulnerability reporting guidance.
make check-ai-adoption-ready, check-ai-project-profile, check-ai-guard-calibration, and ai-cockpit-quality pass on the configured repository.
The configuration diff changes no Rust production behavior, product documentation, business domain, or trading decision logic.
guidelines: Profile facts, suggested boundaries, approved boundaries, unknowns, and approval evidence must remain separate.
Project quality commands must be executable repository commands, not placeholders or no-ops.
CI must use full Git history and bind check-ai-pr to the pull request base commit.

intent.problem: The installed AI Cockpit correctly blocks ordinary Work Items because ORG-X has not completed adopter-specific calibration: no confirmed Project Profile, Coverage review, or hosted quality/check-pr workflow exists.
constraints: Keep AI Cockpit separate from ORG-X business Domain behavior.
Do not change src, tests, Cargo manifests, product documentation, or trading decision boundaries.
Do not infer approvals from detector output; only confirmed Profile fields may satisfy readiness.
Do not add secrets, credentials, or machine-specific paths.
intent.rationale: Completing the explicit adopter configuration gate is required by the installed runtime before WI-002 can start in MODE=code. The smallest safe configuration uses observed Rust facts, confirmed src/tests boundaries, existing Make targets, and a transparent CI workflow.
